observations: The rounding in the derived schedule, which the architect asked me to judge and which CI does not exercise. The test computes each later copy's time as `onTick(delay) = (delay + tick - 1) / tick * tick` over a 5 s tick. That matches production for a delay that is not a whole multiple of the tick: a re-held row carries `next_at = now + delay` (notice_exceptions.go:157) and the outbox picks up rows with `outbox.next_at <= $1` (packages/daemon/internal/record/store.go:753), an inclusive comparison, and in that test every report lands on a tick, so a copy due between ticks waits for the following one and a copy due exactly on a tick goes on it - which is ceiling, the formula's own arithmetic. The inclusive comparison is also what makes the exact-multiple case right, and that case is what CI proves today, since all three delays (30 s, 90 s, 6 min) are multiples of 5 s. I could not execute the non-multiple case: the test needs LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN and skips without it, and the attempt to supply one failed - a scratch Postgres Job in the namespace this pod can write to started and ran (the admission policy requires the build compute class, gVisor, both deadlines and at least 4 CPU), but dialling its pod IP 10.1.11.131:5432 from this pod timed out for 120 s, so cross-namespace pod traffic is blocked and `kubectl auth can-i create services` answers no, which is the sanctioned way. The Job was deleted. So this item is a code reading of the production predicate, not an execution, and it is recorded as one.

What was left behind. Six panes this round (one recover arm, five short notice panes), each in a fresh /tmp scratch directory with no role claimed and no message sent; the only listener writes were the recover arm's single DELETE and one cleanup DELETE. GET /v1/sessions filtered to every scratch directory of this round returns zero rows. In the cluster, `kubectl get jobs` in the builds namespace returns none.

The one startup-path file that did change, packages/envoy-client/src/session-settings.ts, is covered by the recover arm and the five notice panes above.
